topics.t: Constitution Day: 77 years since the Constitution was adopted
topics.news: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) is observed on 26 November, the date in 1949 on which the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution. The day was first notified for yearly observance by the Government in 2015, the year of the 125th birth anniversary of B. R. Ambedkar. In 2026 it marks 77 years since adoption.

rows: Adoption and commencement
Adopted on 26 November 1949; came into force on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day.
Drafting
The Constituent Assembly took about 2 years, 11 months and 18 days. Rajendra Prasad presided over the Assembly and B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.
Parts in force early
Some provisions, such as those on citizenship and elections, took effect on 26 November 1949 itself.
Later additions
Words such as socialist, secular and integrity in the Preamble, and the Fundamental Duties, came through the 42nd Amendment in 1976.

ul: **Why it matters:** the day is used to promote awareness of constitutional values, rights and duties among citizens.

prel.d: The body that framed the Constitution; it first met in December 1946.
The committee under Ambedkar that prepared the draft Constitution.

qs.q: Discuss the significance of the Preamble and how the Constitution has been adapted through amendments since 1950.

topics.t: Rajbanshi language and the Eighth Schedule
topics.news: The West Bengal government has urged the Centre to include the Rajbanshi language in the Eighth Schedule, and Koch Rajbanshi groups have pressed the same demand ahead of the Census. Rajbanshi is an Eastern Indo-Aryan language spoken in parts of Nepal, India and Bangladesh. The Constitution sets no fixed criteria for adding a language to the Schedule.

rows: What it lists
Languages officially recognised by the Union; 22 are listed at present.
Articles
Article 344(1) provides for a commission on the progressive use of Hindi for official purposes; Article 351 directs the Union to promote the spread of Hindi.
Criteria
None fixed in law; the Pahwa Committee (1996) and the Sitakant Mohapatra Committee (2003) looked at the question without an accepted framework.
Recent additions
Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added in 2003 by the 92nd Amendment.

ul: **Why it matters:** inclusion brings recognition, representation in official exams and support for the language.

prel.d: The list of languages recognised in the Constitution.
The language first learnt in childhood, recorded in the Census.

qs.q: Should more languages be added to the Eighth Schedule? Examine the arguments for and against.

topics.t: Valsad Hapus: a separate GI tag sought for a mango variety
topics.news: Gujarat’s Navsari Agricultural University and a farmers’ body have applied to the Geographical Indications Registry for a separate tag for Valsad Hapus, a variety of Alphonso mango. The application is opposed: growers in Maharashtra’s Konkan region object to the use of the name Hapus, saying it could confuse buyers and dilute their own product. Konkan Alphonso has held a GI tag since 2018.

rows: Applicants
A state agricultural university and a farmers’ body in Gujarat applied for a tag for Valsad Hapus; the application is opposed.
Konkan claim
Konkan Hapus holds a GI tag covering five districts of Maharashtra and is valued for export as well as domestic sales.
Objection
A similar name for a product from another region could weaken the reputation tied to the original place.
Legal frame
Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999; a registration is valid for 10 years and can be renewed.

ul: **Why it matters:** GI tags protect regional produce and the incomes linked to it.

prel.d: A sign on goods that have a quality or reputation due to their place of origin.
The office, based in Chennai, that registers geographical indications.

qs.q: What is the role of geographical indications in protecting traditional products and farmer incomes?

topics.t: Colombo Security Conclave: 8th NSA-level meeting held in Malé
topics.news: The 8th National Security Adviser-level meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave was held in Malé in the Maldives. India’s National Security Adviser said the Indian Ocean should connect and not divide nations, stressed the shared maritime ties of the littoral States, and described the grouping as a meeting point of the Neighbourhood First policy and the MAHASAGAR vision. The Conclave was formed in November 2020.

rows: Colombo Security Conclave
A security grouping of Indian Ocean littoral States; India, the Maldives, Sri Lanka, Mauritius, Bangladesh and the Seychelles take part in its meetings.
Five pillars

Maritime safety and security; countering terrorism and radicalisation; fighting trafficking and organised crime; cyber security and protection of critical infrastructure; humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.
MAHASAGAR
Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions, India’s vision for the Indian Ocean.
Neighbourhood First
India’s policy of giving priority to relations with its immediate neighbours.

ul: **Why it matters:** the Conclave lets India lead security cooperation in its maritime neighbourhood.
**Link to policy:** it is a practical expression of Neighbourhood First and of MAHASAGAR.

prel.d: A security grouping of Indian Ocean littoral states that meets at the level of National Security Advisers.
India’s vision for security and growth across the Indian Ocean region.
India’s policy of giving priority to relations with its immediate neighbours.

qs.q: Examine how the Colombo Security Conclave advances India’s maritime security interests in the Indian Ocean region. What are the limits of such minilateral groupings?

topics.t: National Milk Day 2026 at Patna: Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics released
topics.news: The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying marked National Milk Day on 26 November 2026 at Patna in Bihar. The Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2026 were released; they rest on a survey run from March 2025 to February 2026. A dairy processing plant of 2 lakh litres a day at Sikandarpur in Bihta, built with help from the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund, was dedicated, and several other dairy and livestock projects and initiatives were launched. The National Gopal Ratna Awards 2026 were also given.

rows: National Milk Day
Observed on 26 November, the birth anniversary of Verghese Kurien, who led Operation Flood and the cooperative model of Amul.
Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics
The yearly publication of the Department that gives estimates of milk, egg, meat and wool production at national and State levels.
Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund
A fund that supports loans for dairy processing, meat processing and animal feed plants.
Operation Flood
The programme started in 1970 that built a national milk grid and made India the largest milk producer.
National Gopal Ratna Awards
Annual awards for farmers, artificial insemination technicians and dairy cooperatives.

ul: **Why it matters:** dairying gives regular income to small and landless households and is a major source of employment for women.
**Challenge:** milk output growth is argued to be slowing, and yield per animal, feed costs, disease and climate stress remain concerns.

prel.d: A dairy development programme begun in 1970 under the National Dairy Development Board.
The Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund, a credit-linked support scheme.
The electronic livestock integrated sample survey used to collect production data.

qs.q: India is the largest producer of milk, yet productivity per animal is low. Discuss the challenges of the dairy sector and the role of cooperatives in addressing them.

topics.t: India–UAE Joint Defence Cooperation Committee: 14th meeting at Abu Dhabi
topics.news: India and the United Arab Emirates held the 14th meeting of the Joint Defence Cooperation Committee at Abu Dhabi on 26 November 2026. It was co-chaired by India’s Defence Secretary and a senior UAE defence official. The sides agreed to speed up co-development and co-production of next-generation defence equipment and to widen cooperation into the defence industry, artificial intelligence, cyber security, military training and maritime safety. They also agreed to review the progress of ongoing initiatives at regular intervals before the next meeting. The 13th meeting was held in New Delhi in July 2025.

rows: Joint Defence Cooperation Committee
The main institutional forum for defence ties between the two countries; it is held at the level of the Defence Secretary.
Co-development and co-production
Joint design and manufacture of equipment instead of simple purchase, which also supports Make in India.
Strategic partnership
The meeting gave direction to the Strategic Defence Partnership Framework agreed in 2026.
Industry link
The Indian industry delegation visited the Tawazun Industrial Park and met the Tawazun Economic Council.
Wider ties
The two countries have a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement in force since 2022.

ul: **Why it matters:** the UAE is a key energy, trade and investment partner and a gateway to West Asia and Africa for Indian defence exports.
**Way forward:** defence industrial partnership, joint exercises and maritime information sharing can anchor ties during regional instability.

prel.d: Joint manufacture of defence equipment, often with technology sharing.
Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, a broad trade and investment pact.
A framework of regular high-level cooperation across security, economy and technology.

qs.q: Assess the importance of the United Arab Emirates for India’s strategic and defence interests in West Asia.

topics.t: Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat: two years of the campaign against child marriage
topics.news: The Ministry of Women and Child Development announced a national event for 27 November 2026 at New Delhi to mark two years of the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat campaign, which began on 27 November 2024. The event was planned to review progress, recognise grassroots work and highlight what States and Union Territories have done. Citizens and institutions can take a pledge against child marriage on the campaign portal and on public participation platforms. The portal also lets people report cases and find the Child Marriage Prohibition Officer for their area.

rows: Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat
A nationwide campaign for a child-marriage-free India, working through awareness, community mobilisation and reporting.
Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006
Fixes the minimum age of marriage at 18 for women and 21 for men; such marriages are voidable at the option of the child party.
Child Marriage Prohibition Officer
An officer appointed to prevent child marriages, protect victims and collect evidence for prosecution.
Portal
A dedicated platform for reporting incidents, locating officers, recording awareness activities and taking the pledge.
Causes
Poverty, lack of schooling, social norms and safety fears are the main drivers.

ul: **Why it matters:** child marriage harms health, education and rights of girls and is linked with early pregnancy, anaemia and school dropout.
**Way forward:** keep girls in school, make cash and livelihood support available, strengthen local officers and involve panchayats and community groups.

prel.d: An officer under the 2006 Act who prevents child marriages and helps victims.
A marriage that can be set aside at the option of one party.
A Ministry umbrella scheme for the safety and empowerment of women.

qs.q: Despite a strong law, child marriage persists in India. Examine the reasons and evaluate the measures to end it.

topics.t: eSankhyiki State Dashboard: a single window for State-level statistics
topics.news: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation launched a State Dashboard on its eSankhyiki portal on 26 November 2026. It carries 283 indicators drawn from 21 statistical products under 10 themes such as agriculture, education, work and wages, and gender and inclusion. A user can choose a State and see all its indicators, or choose a theme and compare States. Charts, filters, metadata and downloads are provided. The dashboard was built with the Institute for Competitiveness and is part of the Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics and Research (VISTAR), which aims to improve data below the national level.

rows: eSankhyiki
The Ministry’s portal for official statistics, which makes data available in a searchable and downloadable form.
State Dashboard
A tool to see and compare State-level indicators across themes.
VISTAR
Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics and Research, for stronger State, district and local data.
Coverage
283 indicators, 21 statistical products and 10 themes, to be expanded step by step.
Use
Helps State governments, researchers and citizens track outcomes and compare performance.

ul: **Why it matters:** policies for health, education and jobs depend on reliable data below the national level, which has been a weak area.
**Caution:** a dashboard is only as good as the surveys and administrative data behind it, and definitions across sources must match.

prel.d: The Ministry that compiles national accounts, price indices and large sample surveys.
Statistics at the level of States, districts and local bodies.
A named series or survey output, such as a periodic labour force survey.

qs.q: Why is reliable subnational data important for cooperative federalism and evidence-based policy? Discuss the challenges in building it.

topics.t: Supreme Court: a judicial member must confirm attachment under the money-laundering law
topics.news: In Union of India v. J. Sekar, decided on 26 November 2026, the Supreme Court dealt with the structure of the Adjudicating Authority under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The Court held that a bench of the Authority cannot confirm a provisional attachment made by the Enforcement Directorate without a judicial member, though a single-member bench may sit if that member is a judicial member. It held that the Chairperson need not be a judicial member. The Court did not strike down the provisions, but suggested that the Union Government consider repealing the 2009 amendment and going back to the earlier structure with more than one Adjudicating Authority.

rows: Adjudicating Authority
The body under the Act that decides whether property attached by the Enforcement Directorate is involved in money laundering.
Provisional attachment
A temporary attachment of property for a limited period, which the Authority must confirm after hearing the person.
Judicial member
A member with judicial qualifications; the Court held that confirmation needs one on the bench.
Chairperson
The Court held that the head of the Authority need not be a judicial member.
Appeal
Orders of the Authority are appealed to the Appellate Tribunal.

ul: **Why it matters:** attachment affects property rights, so the body that confirms it must have judicial competence.
**Link:** the case belongs to the wider debate on tribunalisation and whether non-judicial members can decide rights-affecting questions.

prel.d: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
A temporary order that freezes property for a limited period.
A quasi-judicial body that decides disputes in a specialised area.

qs.q: Discuss the role of tribunals in the Indian justice system. How far should non-judicial members be allowed to decide questions affecting property and liberty?

topics.t: Supreme Court: a possible disqualification cannot be the main ground to stay a legislator’s conviction
topics.news: In State of Karnataka v. Vinay Rajashekharappa Kulkarni, decided on 26 November 2026, the Supreme Court held that a stay of conviction needs a palpable mistake in the judgment that makes it illegal, and that the prospect of disqualification of a legislator cannot be the primary reason for a stay. The Court set aside the High Court’s stay orders. It reasoned that if disqualification alone were enough, every convicted legislator would get a stay.

rows: Section 8(3), Representation of the People Act, 1951
A person convicted and sentenced to at least two years’ imprisonment is disqualified from the date of conviction and for six years after release.
Lily Thomas (2013)
The Court struck down Section 8(4), which had given sitting legislators three months to appeal before disqualification.
Stay of conviction
Only a stay of the conviction, not just of the sentence, can suspend the disqualification.
Palpable mistake
A clear and evident error that makes the judgment illegal; an arguable case is not enough.
Constitutional basis
Articles 102(1)(e) and 191(1)(e) allow disqualification by law of members of Parliament and State legislatures.

ul: **Why it matters:** it prevents the stay of conviction from becoming a routine way for convicted legislators to keep their seats.
**Link:** it supports the aim of keeping criminality out of politics while leaving appeal rights intact.

prel.d: An order that suspends the effect of a conviction pending appeal.
The 2013 judgment that struck down protection from immediate disqualification for sitting legislators.
The provision that disqualifies a person sentenced to two years or more.

qs.q: Discuss the legal framework for disqualification of convicted legislators in India. Is the present law sufficient to curb criminalisation of politics?

topics.t: Foodgrain output at a record 378.54 million tonnes in 2025–26
topics.news: The final estimates of crop production for 2025–26 put foodgrain output at a record 3,785.38 lakh tonnes (378.54 million tonnes), which is about 208 lakh tonnes more than in the previous year. Final estimates are made after crop cutting experiments and revise the earlier advance and second and third advance estimates.

rows: Advance estimates
Early estimates of crop output made in stages during the year; they are revised as sowing and yield data come in.
Crop cutting experiments
Sample harvests in fields used to measure yield per hectare, which feed the final estimates.
Kharif and rabi
Kharif crops are sown with the monsoon and harvested in autumn; rabi crops are sown in winter.

ul: **Why it matters:** estimates guide procurement, buffer stocks, trade policy and price management.
**Concern:** a record harvest does not remove climate risk; irrigation, drought-proof seeds and crop insurance are needed.

prel.d: Early stage-wise forecasts of crop production.
A climate pattern that warms the central and eastern Pacific and can weaken the Indian monsoon.
A crop sown at the start of the monsoon, such as rice, maize and cotton.

qs.q: How do El Niño and monsoon variability affect India’s agriculture? Suggest measures to build climate resilience in foodgrain production.

topics.t: Chariot-1 foundation models launched under the IndiaAI Mission
topics.news: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology launched the Chariot-1 foundation models at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on 26 November 2026. The suite has a large language model and a text-to-speech model, trained from scratch in India by a Delhi-based company that is among the first teams chosen under the IndiaAI Mission to build sovereign foundation models. The launch is presented as a step towards strengthening indigenous AI capability.

rows: IndiaAI Mission
A national mission that supports computing capacity, datasets, skills and indigenous foundation models.
Foundation model
A large model trained on broad data that can be adapted to many tasks.
Large language model
A model that learns patterns in text and can generate and understand language.
Text-to-speech
Technology that turns written text into spoken audio.
Sovereign AI
Building models and infrastructure within the country, for data control and local needs.

ul: **Why it matters:** home-grown models can serve Indian languages and reduce dependence on foreign technology.
**Challenge:** access to chips, quality data, energy and talent, and safeguards on misuse and bias.

prel.d: A broad pre-trained model that can be adapted for many tasks.
The national programme to build AI compute, data and models in India.
AI systems built and controlled within a country.

qs.q: What is the case for building sovereign foundation models in India? Discuss the challenges and the role of public policy.

topics.t: United States trade probe on excess manufacturing capacity: India says it has none
topics.news: The government said it is examining a determination by the United States Trade Representative in an investigation under Section 301 of the Trade Act on alleged structural excess capacity in manufacturing across 14 economies, India among them. India's Department of Commerce told the investigators that India has no structural excess capacity in any sector, and India wants trade concerns settled within the continuing bilateral trade agreement talks.

rows: Section 301
A provision of the United States Trade Act of 1974 that lets the country investigate and act against trade practices it considers unfair.
Structural excess capacity
Production capacity that is persistently larger than domestic demand, so surplus output is pushed into export markets.
India's position
No such capacity exists in any sector; concerns belong in the bilateral trade agreement negotiations.
Timeline of talks
A trade announcement was made on 2 February 2026 and a joint statement followed on 7 February 2026.
Scope
The probe covers 14 economies, not India alone.

ul: **Why it matters:** tariffs and trade remedies directly affect Indian exports such as textiles, gems, engineering goods and farm products.
**Way forward:** India wants an early conclusion of the trade agreement while keeping its position on sensitive sectors.

prel.d: US law allowing investigations and trade action against unfair foreign practices.
A pact between two countries that sets tariffs and market access terms.

qs.q: Unilateral trade measures by major economies challenge the rules-based trading system. Analyse the implications for India.
